mentions.name: Cargo for C
mentions.description: A Cargo-like build tool and package manager for C. It gives C projects a TOML manifest and build scripts written in C that the tool JIT-compiles, provides a stable ABI, an HTTP-backed package index and a Git-backed package index, and builds dependencies natively instead of wrapping their Make or CMake files. It aims to let users run C files from source, generate single-file static binaries, and dynamically link against older glibc without arcane tricks.
mentions.problem: Building C code requires pulling in Python or Lua for the build system, and the author considers CMake and the surrounding ecosystem painful.
mentions.source_excerpt: I am making Cargo for C. I have 3/4 of a working demo; the tool can build itself, including some non-trivial dependencies which I've ported to build natively with the tool (instead of wrapping their Make or CMake or whatever).
